mainTopic: Testing the claim of שמואל and רבי אלעזר that the הלכה follows רבי אליעזר in only four cases: what the count covers, and which cases do not count.
overview: שמואל said the הלכה follows רבי אליעזר in only four cases. The גמרא challenges this from the מיאון case in יבמות, and answers that the four are only in סדר טהרות. It supports this with a case about חלה, then asks why that case is a better proof. The answer it settles on: in the מיאון case, רבי יהודה בן בבא agrees with רבי אליעזר, as a ברייתא's careful plural 'minor girls' shows. Next, רבי אלעזר makes the same 'four cases' statement. Here the סדר טהרות answer fails: רבי זירא's remark about balsam shows that רבי אלעזר's four cover the whole משנה. So the מיאון case is again explained away because רבי יהודה בן בבא agrees with רבי אליעזר. Finally, רבי אלעזר's ruling about saying הבדלה in הודאה does not count either, because רבי אליעזר was repeating רבי חנינא בן גמליאל.

steps.title: The challenge from the minor's refusal case ends
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its challenge: in the יבמות case, רבי אליעזר says we teach the קטנה to refuse, and שמואל rules like him. So how can שמואל say there are only four such cases?
steps.simpleTranslation: [רבי אליעזר says:] We teach the minor girl to refuse him. And רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: the הלכה follows רבי אליעזר! (So there is a fifth case.)
steps.whatsHappening: This is the end of a challenge that began just before this passage. The גמרא shows a case outside the 'four' where שמואל still rules like רבי אליעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל said the הלכה follows רבי אליעזר in only four cases. Here is a case in יבמות where he also rules like רבי אליעזר. That seems to contradict the 'only four' claim.

keyTerms.meaning: We teach / instruct (the court guides her)
A girl under בת מצוה age, married off under rabbinic law
Refusal: a minor girl cancels her rabbinic marriage by declaring she does not want her husband
The practical law follows this opinion

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up רבי אליעזר (the main figure here) with רבי אלעזר, who comes up later in this passage. The names look almost the same but they are different people. Later on there is even a רבי אלעזר who is a תנא and another who is an אמורא.

phrases.english: We teach the minor girl to refuse him,
phrases.notes: These are רבי אליעזר's words, quoted from a משנה in יבמות. The challenge began just before this line.

phrases.english: and Rav Yehuda said in the name of Shmuel:
The halakha follows Rabbi Eliezer!
phrases.notes: The exclamation means: so here is another case beyond the four!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge to שמואל's 'only four cases' rule that began before this passage.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's statement that the הלכה follows רבי אליעזר in only four cases.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A fifth case exists (מיאון in יבמות) where שמואל rules like רבי אליעזר, so 'only four' seems false.

steps.title: The four cases are only within סדר טהרות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that שמואל's 'four cases' meant four in סדר טהרות. In the other סדרים there are many cases where the הלכה follows רבי אליעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: When שמואל said the הלכה follows רבי אליעזר in four cases, he meant four in סדר טהרות. In the other סדרים there are many.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by narrowing what שמואל meant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The limit of 'four' was never about all of ש"ס, only about the order of purity laws. The יבמות case is in סדר נשים, so it does not count against the four. The challenge falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: The order of the משנה dealing with ritual purity
The other orders of the משנה
There are many

steps.whatToRemember: שמואל's 'only four' applies only to סדר טהרות. Outside it, the הלכה follows רבי אליעזר many times.

phrases.english: When Shmuel said
the halakha follows Rabbi Eliezer in four cases,
he meant in Seder Teharot;
but in the other orders there are many.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the original statement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought 'four cases' meant four in all of ש"ס.
steps.terutzMaskana: It means four within סדר טהרות only. Elsewhere there are many.

steps.title: Support from the case of חלה and the basket
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא backs up the answer: in a משנה about חלה, which is not in סדר טהרות, רבי אליעזר says a basket combines loaves for חלה, and שמואל rules like him.
steps.simpleTranslation: This also makes sense, since we learned: רבי אליעזר says even someone who takes loaves out of the oven and puts them in a basket, the basket joins them together for the obligation of חלה. And רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: the הלכה follows רבי אליעזר. Learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second case outside סדר טהרות where שמואל rules like רבי אליעזר, to show the answer is correct.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If שמואל's 'four' covered all of ש"ס, this חלה case would be another contradiction. Since שמואל clearly rules like רבי אליעזר here, his 'four' must have been limited to סדר טהרות.

keyTerms.meaning: And this is also logical: it introduces support for an answer
One who takes bread out of the oven
The basket joins them together into one amount
The portion of dough given to a כהן
Learn from this: the proof is accepted

phrases.english: And this is also logical,
as we learned: Rabbi Eliezer says:
Even one who takes loaves out of the oven and puts them into a basket,
phrases.notes: Each loaf alone is too small to need חלה. The question is whether the basket makes them count as one.

phrases.english: the basket combines them for the obligation of challa.
And Rav Yehuda said in the name of Shmuel:
The halakha follows Rabbi Eliezer.
Learn from this.
phrases.notes: Learn that שמואל's 'four' only meant four in סדר טהרות.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer given in step 2.
steps.raayaObject: That שמואל's 'four cases' is limited to סדר טהרות.
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in חלה (2:4): the basket combines loaves; שמואל rules like רבי אליעזר.

steps.title: Why is the חלה case a better proof than the יבמות case?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: the יבמות case was also outside סדר טהרות. Why is the חלה case a stronger proof than the original one?
steps.simpleTranslation: And what makes this case stronger than that one?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the proof it just brought. It sets up an explanation of why the two cases are different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both the יבמות case and the חלה case are outside סדר טהרות, and in both שמואל rules like רבי אליעזר. So why was the יבמות case treated as a challenge, while the חלה case is called a supporting proof? The גמרא wants to know what makes חלה more convincing.

keyTerms.meaning: What makes this one stronger than that one?

phrases.english: And what makes this case stronger than that one?
phrases.notes: 'This' is the חלה case; 'that' is the minor's refusal case from step 1.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions why the proof in step 3 is better than the case in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the חלה case adds support beyond the יבמות case.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both cases are outside סדר טהרות, so neither seems stronger than the other.

steps.title: In the יבמות case, רבי אלעזר agrees with רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: The יבמות case is weaker because רבי אלעזר holds the same view, as a משנה shows. In חלה, רבי אליעזר stands alone, so שמואל's ruling there is clearly a ruling like רבי אליעזר himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because רבי אלעזר holds like him there. As we learned: רבי אלעזר says, we teach the minor girl to refuse him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the חלה case is the better proof, and quotes a משנה to show that רבי אלעזר agrees in the refusal case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the refusal case, another תנא, רבי אלעזר, says the same thing. So someone could say שמואל was not really ruling like רבי אליעזר alone. In the חלה case nobody else agrees with רבי אליעזר, so it clearly shows שמואל ruling like רבי אליעזר outside סדר טהרות.

keyTerms.meaning: Stands with him / holds the same view

steps.confusionAlert: רבי אלעזר (here) is not רבי אליעזר. The point is that a second, different תנא agrees with רבי אליעזר in the יבמות case.
steps.whatToRemember: The חלה case is the stronger proof because רבי אליעזר is alone there. In the refusal case, רבי אלעזר says the same thing.

phrases.english: Because Rabbi Elazar holds like him there.
As we learned: Rabbi Elazar says:
We teach the minor girl to refuse him.
phrases.notes: These are the same words רבי אליעזר used in step 1, now said by רבי אלעזר in a different משנה in יבמות.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 4.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The יבמות case and the חלה case seem equally strong.
steps.terutzMaskana: The יבמות case is weaker because רבי אלעזר agrees there. The חלה case shows רבי אליעזר's view alone being followed.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that when another תנא agrees, a ruling 'like רבי אליעזר' may not really count as a ruling for him alone.

steps.title: Do רבי אלעזר and רבי אליעזר really say the same thing?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא attacks the answer from step 5. Elsewhere it explains that the rulings of רבי אליעזר and רבי אלעזר are each needed because they deal with different cases. So רבי אלעזר does not really stand with רבי אליעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: But does he really stand with him? Don't we explain that both rulings are needed, because they are not alike?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges its own last answer. It says רבי אלעזר does not truly hold like רבי אליעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 5 said שמואל's ruling in יבמות is weaker proof because רבי אלעזר shares רבי אליעזר's view. But if each ruling is needed because each covers a different case, then the two are not the same opinion. So רבי אליעזר is really alone here, and the answer from step 5 falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: And does he stand (agree)? A challenge asking whether one sage truly holds like another
We explain that both are needed, because each teaches something the other does not
They are not similar to each other

phrases.english: But does he really stand with him?
phrases.notes: He means: does רבי אלעזר really hold like רבי אליעזר, as step 5 claimed?

phrases.english: But don't we explain that both of them are needed,
phrases.notes: This points to the discussion in מסכת יבמות, where each ruling is shown to teach something different.

phrases.english: and they are not similar to each other!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי קָאֵי? וְהָא אַצְרוֹכֵי מַצְרְכִינַן לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer given in step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim from step 5 that רבי אלעזר holds the same view as רבי אליעזר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If each ruling is needed because each covers a different case, then the two sages do not share one opinion, so רבי אלעזר is no backup for רבי אליעזר.

steps.title: New answer: רבי יהודה בן בבא agrees with רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops the old answer and gives a new one. The יבמות case is weaker proof because a different sage, רבי יהודה בן בבא, holds like רבי אליעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is because רבי יהודה בן בבא stands with him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new reason why the יבמות case is a weaker proof. The next step brings the source for this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point is the same as before: if another sage agrees with רבי אליעזר, then שמואל might be following that other sage, not רבי אליעזר himself. Only the name of the agreeing sage changes. Now it is רבי יהודה בן בבא instead of רבי אלעזר.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. It drops the earlier answer and brings a new one
Stands like him, meaning he holds the same opinion

phrases.english: Rather, it is because there stands
Rabbi Yehuda ben Bava, holding like him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, מִשּׁוּם דְּקָאֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בָּבָא כְּוָתֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the answer that step 6 knocked down.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Replacement answer: a different sage shares רבי אליעזר's view
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The יבמות case was weaker because רבי אלעזר agreed with רבי אליעזר.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is weaker because רבי יהודה בן בבא agrees with רבי אליעזר, so שמואל's ruling may not be following רבי אליעזר alone.

steps.title: The five testimonies of רבי יהודה בן בבא
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא lists five things רבי יהודה בן בבא testified about. The first is that we have minor girls do מיאון. The other four are unrelated rulings that come along with the list.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: רבי יהודה בן בבא testified about five things. That we have minor girls refuse. That we let a woman remarry based on one witness. That a rooster was stoned in Jerusalem for killing a person. About forty-day-old wine poured on the altar. And about the morning תמיד offered at four hours into the day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source for its new answer: a ברייתא with five testimonies of רבי יהודה בן בבא. Only the first one, about minor girls doing מיאון, matters for our discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא shows that רבי יהודה בן בבא held that we have minor girls do מיאון. This is the same subject as the יבמות case where רבי אליעזר rules this way. The next step will look closely at the plural word 'girls' to tie him to רבי אליעזר.

keyTerms.meaning: Testified, meaning he reported a ruling he had received
Have them do מיאון: a girl married off as a minor by her mother or brothers declares she refuses the marriage
One witness, here enough to let a woman remarry
Was stoned (put to death by stoning)
The daily morning offering in the בית המקדש

steps.confusionAlert: Do not get stuck on the rooster, the wine and the תמיד. They are just part of the list. The גמרא only needs the first item, about minor girls.

phrases.english: As it was taught in a baraita:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בָּבָא הֵעִיד חֲמִשָּׁה דְּבָרִים:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda ben Bava testified about five things:
that we have the minor girls refuse.
And that we let a woman remarry
based on one witness,
phrases.notes: One witness who says her husband died.

phrases.english: and that a rooster was stoned in Jerusalem
for killing a person,
and about forty-day-old wine
that was poured as a libation on the altar,
and about the daily morning offering
that was offered at four hours into the day.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא, רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בָּבָא הֵעִיד חֲמִשָּׁה דְּבָרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source for the claim in step 7.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יהודה בן בבא holds like רבי אליעזר on having minor girls do מיאון.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא listing the five testimonies of רבי יהודה בן בבא, starting with 'שֶׁמְּמָאֲנִים אֶת הַקְּטַנּוֹת'.

steps.title: Reading 'minor girls' as the two cases of רבי אלעזר and רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points to the plural word 'minor girls'. It suggests this means two girls: the one in רבי אלעזר's ruling and the one in רבי אליעזר's ruling. If so, רבי יהודה בן בבא agrees with רבי אליעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is meant by 'minor girls'? Isn't it one girl from רבי אלעזר's case and one from רבי אליעזר's case?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to finish its proof by reading the plural word 'girls' in the ברייתא closely.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plural seems to cover two separate rulings about minor girls. One is רבי אלעזר's case and one is רבי אליעזר's case. That would show רבי יהודה בן בבא holds like רבי אליעזר, which backs up the answer in step 7.

keyTerms.meaning: Minor girls (plural). The whole argument hangs on this plural word
Is it not? This sets up a suggested reading
One... and one, meaning two separate cases

phrases.english: What is meant by 'minor girls'?
Is it not one girl from Rabbi Elazar's case,
and one from Rabbi Eliezer's case?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי קְטַנּוֹת? לָאו חֲדָא דְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reads the ברייתא from step 8 closely to complete the proof for step 7.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יהודה בן בבא holds like רבי אליעזר.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The plural word 'קְטַנּוֹת' in the ברייתא, read as two cases: רבי אלעזר's and רבי אליעזר's.

steps.title: 'Minor girls' may just mean minor girls in general
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the reading from step 9. The plural 'minor girls' does not have to mean two specific rulings. It can simply mean minor girls in general, so there is no proof that רבי יהודה בן בבא holds like רבי אליעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. What does 'minor girls' mean? Minor girls in general.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on its own proof. The plural word does not prove what we wanted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 9 needed the plural to point to two different cases. But a plural can also just describe the general group, meaning any minor girls in such a situation. Once that reading is possible, the ברייתא no longer shows that רבי יהודה בן בבא agrees with רבי אליעזר specifically.

keyTerms.meaning: Of the world, meaning in general, ordinary

steps.whatToRemember: The גמרא is checking why the יבמות case is a weaker proof than the חלה case. רבי אלעזר did not work (step 6), and the proof that רבי יהודה בן בבא agrees with רבי אליעזר has just been pushed back. Steps 11-12 bring it back.

phrases.english: No. What does 'minor girls' mean?
Minor girls in general.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the reading of the ברייתא offered in step 9.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof from the plural word 'קְטַנּוֹת' that רבי יהודה בן בבא holds like רבי אליעזר.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The plural can simply mean minor girls in general. It does not have to refer to two separate cases, one from each sage.

steps.title: Then why does the list say 'a woman' and not 'women'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא attacks the rejection from step 10. If plurals just mean 'in general', the ברייתא should also have said 'women' in its ruling about a woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, then in the ruling about a woman, let it also say 'women', and we would explain it as women in general!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back against step 10. Step 10 said 'minor girls' could just mean girls in general.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same list of רבי יהודה בן בבא's testimonies has a ruling about a woman, written in the singular. If the ברייתא used plurals for 'in general', it would have said 'women' there too. Since it did not, the plural 'minor girls' looks deliberate.

keyTerms.meaning: If so — if we accept what you just said
Let it teach — the ברייתא should have said
In general — of the world at large

phrases.english: If so,
regarding 'a woman' as well,
phrases.notes: This is another item on רבי יהודה בן בבא's list: a woman may remarry based on one witness.

phrases.english: let it teach 'women'
and we would say: women in general!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the rejection in step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: Step 10's claim that 'minor girls' just means girls in general.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same ברייתא uses the singular 'a woman' elsewhere. So it does not use plurals casually.

steps.title: The plural is precise, so רבי יהודה בן בבא agrees with רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: Because the list says 'a woman' in one place and 'minor girls' in another, the plural must be exact. It refers to two girls, so the proof from step 9 stands.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, since here it says 'a woman' and here it says 'minor girls', learn from this that it is speaking precisely. Indeed, learn from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא concludes that 'minor girls' was said on purpose. The proof from step 9 comes back and is accepted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Singular for the woman and plural for the girls shows the wording is careful. So 'minor girls' means the two girls in the rulings of רבי אלעזר and רבי אליעזר. That means רבי יהודה בן בבא agrees with רבי אליעזר.

keyTerms.meaning: Precisely — said on purpose, exactly as worded
Learn from it — the point is proven
Minor girls (plural)

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא's choice of singular and plural is exact. So רבי יהודה בן בבא holds like רבי אליעזר in the מיאון case.

phrases.english: Rather, since here it teaches 'a woman',
and here it teaches 'minor girls',
learn from it that it is teaching precisely.
Indeed, learn from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the challenge in step 11 and brings back the proof of step 9.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: 'Minor girls' refers to the two specific girls, so רבי יהודה בן בבא agrees with רבי אליעזר.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: the הלכה follows רבי אליעזר in four cases
steps.stepSummary: A new statement: רבי אלעזר says the הלכה follows רבי אליעזר in four cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: And similarly רבי אלעזר said: the הלכה follows רבי אליעזר in four cases.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new section with a statement from רבי אלעזר. It is setting up the questions that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר's views are usually not followed. רבי אלעזר gives an exact number: only four times is the הלכה like him. The next steps test whether that number holds up.

keyTerms.meaning: The practical law follows the opinion of...
In four (cases)

phrases.english: And similarly, Rabbi Elazar said:
The halacha follows Rabbi Eliezer in four cases.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a parallel discussion. 'וְכֵן' links רבי אלעזר's statement to שמואל's identical 'four cases' rule discussed in steps 1-12, and the גמרא now tests it the same way.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows רבי אליעזר in exactly four cases.

steps.title: Isn't the מיאון ruling a fifth case?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: are there really no more than four? רבי אלעזר also ruled like רבי אליעזר about teaching a minor girl to refuse.
steps.simpleTranslation: And there are no more? But we learned in a משנה: רבי אליעזר says we teach the minor girl to refuse him. And רבי אלעזר said the הלכה follows רבי אליעזר!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the number four. It points to another place where רבי אלעזר ruled like רבי אליעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the מיאון case, רבי אלעזר himself ruled like רבי אליעזר. If that case is outside the four, then there are at least five, which contradicts 'four'.

keyTerms.meaning: And there are no more?
We instruct / teach
That she should refuse (do מיאון)

phrases.english: And there are no more?
But didn't we learn:
Rabbi Eliezer says
we instruct the minor girl to refuse him,
phrases.notes: Through מיאון, a girl married off as a minor ends the marriage by refusing her husband.

phrases.english: and Rabbi Elazar said:
The halacha follows Rabbi Eliezer!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the count in step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר's claim of only four cases.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another ruling of his, about מיאון, also follows רבי אליעזר. That makes more than four.

steps.title: Suggestion: the four are only in סדר טהרות
steps.stepSummary: A possible answer: maybe רבי אלעזר meant four cases in סדר טהרות only, and the other סדרים have more.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you would say: when רבי אלעזר said the הלכה follows רבי אליעזר in four cases, he meant in סדר טהרות, but in the other סדרים there are more.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a possible way out of the question. It is setting this up so that it can test the idea next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'four' is limited to סדר טהרות, then the מיאון ruling (in סדר נשים) does not contradict it. But this answer only works if other סדרים really have more such cases, and that is what the גמרא checks next.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you would say — introduces a possible answer
The order of the משנה dealing with purity
The other orders of the משנה

phrases.english: And if you would say:
when Rabbi Elazar said
the halacha follows Rabbi Eliezer in four
he meant in Seder Taharot,
but in the other orders there are more.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵימָא: כִּי אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proposes an answer to the challenge in step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the statement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Four' seemed to mean four in all of the משנה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Maybe it means four in סדר טהרות alone.

steps.title: Are there really more? The balsam משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא doubts the suggestion and brings a משנה from שביעית. רבי פדת says its ruling that balsam is a fruit follows רבי אליעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: But are there really more? We learned: the rose, henna, rockrose and balsam have the holiness of שביעית, and so does the money paid for them. They must be removed (ביעור), and so must the money paid for them. And רבי פדת said: who taught that balsam is a fruit? רבי אליעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions whether other סדרים really have more cases. It brings a test case from סדר זרעים to check.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי פדת says the view that balsam counts as a fruit, and so has שביעית holiness, belongs to רבי אליעזר. The next step shows what follows from this for the count of four.

keyTerms.meaning: But are there? (doubting the claim)
The holiness of produce of the seventh year
Removal of seventh-year produce from one's home at the set time
Balsam
A fruit

phrases.english: But are there?
But didn't we learn:
phrases.notes: משנה שביעית 7:6.

phrases.english: the rose and the henna,
and the rockrose and the balsam
have the holiness of the seventh year, and so does the money paid for them,
they must be removed, and so must the money paid for them.
And Rabbi Pedat said:
Who taught that balsam is a fruit?
phrases.notes: He means the sap of the balsam tree counts as its fruit, so it gets שביעית holiness.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts to reject the suggestion of step 15.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The idea that other סדרים have more cases where the הלכה follows רבי אליעזר.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A ruling of רבי אליעזר in סדר זרעים is treated as not being the הלכה, as the next step shows.

steps.title: רבי זירא: between father and son, balsam is permitted
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא tells רבי פדת that together with his father רבי אלעזר he has freed balsam from שביעית. The balsam ruling is רבי אליעזר's, and it is not among the four cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי זירא said: see how between you and your father you have permitted balsam to the world! You said: who taught that balsam is a fruit? רבי אליעזר. And your father said: the הלכה follows רבי אליעזר in four cases.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא combines the father's and the son's statements. His remark assumes that רבי אלעזר's 'four' covers all the סדרים, not just טהרות. The גמרא proves that next, from רבי פדת's silence.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי פדת said the balsam ruling is רבי אליעזר's. His father רבי אלעזר said the הלכה follows רבי אליעזר in only four cases. Since balsam is not one of the four, it does not follow the הלכה, so balsam has no שביעית holiness. This assumes the four count applies outside טהרות too. If it were only about טהרות, רבי פדת could have said so, and since he didn't, the suggestion that it covers only טהרות falls.

keyTerms.meaning: You (plural) have permitted
See / look
Your father

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אלעזר's 'four cases' covers the whole משנה, not just סדר טהרות. That is why balsam ends up permitted.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי זירא's main point is what their two statements lead to when you put them together.
steps.whyThisMatters: It cancels the escape of step 15. So the question from the מיאון case in step 14 comes back. Steps 19-22 answer it.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Zeira said:
see that from you and from your father,
phrases.notes: He is talking to רבי פדת, whose father is רבי אלעזר.

phrases.english: you have permitted balsam to the world!
You said:

phrases.aramaic: מַאן תַּנָּא קִטְפָא פֵּירָא? רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר,
phrases.english: Who taught that balsam is a fruit? Rabbi Eliezer,
and your father said:
The halacha follows Rabbi Eliezer in four cases.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא: חֲזִי דְּמִינָּךְ וּמֵאֲבוּךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the rejection begun in step 16 by drawing out what follows from the balsam source.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי אלעזר's four cases cover the whole משנה, not only סדר טהרות.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי זירא's remark joining רבי פדת's statement with רבי אלעזר's.

steps.title: If it were only about טהרות, רבי פדת would have said so
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains why the 'only in סדר טהרות' answer fails. If it were true, רבי פדת could have told רבי זירא that his father's four cases were limited to טהרות.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it were true, רבי פדת should have answered: when my father said the הלכה follows רבי אליעזר in four cases, he meant four in סדר טהרות, but in the other סדרים there are more.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes knocking down the suggestion from step 15. רבי פדת had an easy answer available, and he did not use it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי זירא was surprised that the balsam ruling was not among the four cases. If the four were limited to טהרות, רבי פדת could have simply said so. His silence shows the four cases cover all of ש״ס, so the suggestion is rejected.

keyTerms.meaning: And if it were so (if the suggestion were true)
The order of the משנה dealing with purity laws
The other orders of the משנה
The practical law follows the opinion of

phrases.english: And if it is so,
phrases.notes: He means: if the four cases were really only about טהרות, as step 15 suggested.

phrases.english: let him say to him:
phrases.notes: Let רבי פדת answer רבי זירא this way.

phrases.english: When my father said
the halacha follows Rabbi Eliezer in four
in Seder Taharos,
but in the other orders there are more.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the רבי זירא and רבי פדת exchange and uses it to reject step 15.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Fully rejects the idea that the four cases are limited to סדר טהרות.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי פדת did not answer with this easy reply, so the limitation cannot be correct.

steps.title: The minor girl case is a problem again
steps.stepSummary: With the טהרות answer gone, the original problem from step 14 comes back. The ruling about the minor girl seems to be a fifth case.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then that case is difficult!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to its earlier problem. רבי אלעזר also ruled like רבי אליעזר about teaching a minor to refuse, so how can there be only four cases?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 15 had tried to solve this by limiting the four to טהרות. That answer was just rejected, so the minor girl ruling again looks like an extra case that does not fit the count.

keyTerms.meaning: A difficulty, an unanswered problem
That one (the case mentioned earlier)

phrases.english: But then that case is difficult!
phrases.notes: 'That case' is the ruling about teaching a minor girl to refuse, from step 14.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 15's answer is rejected, the challenge from step 14 returns.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר's statement that he ruled like רבי אליעזר in only four cases.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The minor girl ruling would be a fifth case, and there is no longer a way to exclude it.

steps.title: The תנא רבי אלעזר agrees in the minor girl case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the minor girl ruling does not count. There, the הלכה is decided because the תנא רבי אלעזר agrees with רבי אליעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: It does not count, because רבי אלעזר the תנא agrees with him. As we learned in a משנה: רבי אלעזר says, we teach the minor girl to refuse him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the problem. The four cases are places where רבי אליעזר stands alone. In the minor girl case, another תנא holds the same way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that the count of four includes only rulings that follow רבי אליעזר by himself. When another תנא agrees with him, the ruling is not really 'like רבי אליעזר' alone. So it is not one of the four.

keyTerms.meaning: Stands with him, holds like his opinion
We teach / instruct (the court advises her)
A girl under the age of מצוות
Refusal: a minor girl married off by her mother or brothers can reject the marriage

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up three names! רבי אליעזר is the תנא in the four cases. רבי אלעזר the אמורא, who is רבי פדת's father, made the 'four cases' statement. Here, 'רבי אלעזר אומר' in the משנה is a different person, a תנא.

phrases.english: Because Rabbi Elazar holds like him,
phrases.notes: This רבי אלעזר is the תנא from the משנה, not the אמורא who said 'four cases.'

phrases.english: as we learned: Rabbi Elazar says:
We instruct the minor girl
to refuse him.
phrases.notes: 'Him' is her husband. By refusing, she ends the marriage.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the count: only cases where רבי אליעזר stands alone are counted.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every ruling like רבי אליעזר should count toward the four.
steps.terutzMaskana: A ruling where another תנא (רבי אלעזר) agrees with him is not counted.

steps.title: But רבי אלעזר's opinion is different from רבי אליעזר's
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer. The גמרא elsewhere showed that both opinions are needed, so they are not the same view.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does he really hold like him? Don't we explain that both statements are needed, and they are not like each other?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from step 20. It argues that the תנא רבי אלעזר does not really hold the same as רבי אליעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If both statements had to be taught separately, each one must say something the other does not. So they are different opinions. That means רבי אלעזר does not really 'stand with' רבי אליעזר, and the answer falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: And does he really hold that way? (a challenging question)
We explain that both statements are necessary
They are not similar to each other

phrases.english: And does he really hold like him?
But don't we explain that both are necessary,
phrases.notes: This points to a discussion in מסכת יבמות showing that each opinion teaches something the other does not.

phrases.english: and they are not like each other!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי קָאֵי, וְהָא אַצְרוֹכֵי מַצְרְכִינַן לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the תנא רבי אלעזר agrees with רבי אליעזר in the minor girl case.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Elsewhere the גמרא shows both opinions are needed, which proves they are different. So רבי אלעזר does not truly agree.

steps.title: רבי יהודה בן בבא agrees instead
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a new answer. In the minor girl case, it is רבי יהודה בן בבא who agrees with רבי אליעזר, so the case is not counted.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is because רבי יהודה בן בבא holds like him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא replaces its rejected answer with a better one. It keeps the same rule, that a case does not count when another תנא agrees. It just names a different תנא who agrees.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The basic idea from step 20 stays. The four cases are only places where רבי אליעזר stands alone. The minor girl case is still left out, but now because of רבי יהודה בן בבא, not the תנא רבי אלעזר.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (rejects the last idea and offers a new one)
Because
A sage of the משנה period

steps.whatToRemember: The 'four cases' are places where the הלכה follows רבי אליעזר even though he stands alone. In the minor girl case, רבי יהודה בן בבא agrees with him, so it does not count.

phrases.english: Rather, it is because there stands
Rabbi Yehuda ben Bava, holding like him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מִשּׁוּם דְּקָאֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בָּבָא כְּוָותֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a new answer after step 21 knocked down the answer of step 20.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The תנא רבי אלעזר is the one who agrees with רבי אליעזר.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יהודה בן בבא is the one who agrees, so the case is left out of the four.

steps.title: Another case: where to say הבדלה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא raises a new problem. רבי אלעזר also ruled like רבי אליעזר about saying הבדלה in the ברכה of הודאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Are there really no more? But we learned: רבי עקיבא says, one says it as a fourth ברכה by itself. רבי אליעזר says, one says it in the ברכה of thanks. And רבי אלעזר said: the הלכה follows רבי אליעזר!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new challenge to the 'only four cases' statement. It brings a משנה about where to say הבדלה, where רבי אלעזר also ruled like רבי אליעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here רבי אליעזר seems to stand alone against רבי עקיבא. So the trick from step 22 does not seem to work. The case looks like a real fifth case, which contradicts רבי אלעזר's count.

keyTerms.meaning: And are there no more?
The prayer that separates שבת or יום טוב from the weekday
A fourth ברכה: for רבי עקיבא, a new separate ברכה just for הבדלה
By itself, as a separate ברכה
The ברכה of thanks (מודים) in שמונה עשרה

phrases.english: And are there no more?
But didn't we learn: Rabbi Akiva says:
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in מסכת ברכות about saying הבדלה on מוצאי שבת.

phrases.english: One says it as a fourth blessing by itself,
phrases.notes: 'It' means הבדלה. The words leave it out because the משנה already spoke about it.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says: one says it in the blessing of thanks,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר!
phrases.english: and Rabbi Elazar said: the halacha follows Rabbi Eliezer!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the minor girl case is settled, the גמרא brings a new case that challenges the count of four.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר's statement that the הלכה follows רבי אליעזר in only four cases.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי אלעזר also ruled like רבי אליעזר about הבדלה, which is not one of the four. That would make it a fifth case.

steps.title: The הבדלה ruling was said in the name of רבי חנינא בן גמליאל
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא answers that the הבדלה-in-הודאה ruling does not count as a case of following רבי אליעזר. רבי אליעזר was only repeating what רבי חנינא בן גמליאל taught, and a ברייתא shows this was רבי חנינא בן גמליאל's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא said: That ruling does not count, because רבי אליעזר said it in the name of רבי חנינא בן גמליאל. A ברייתא teaches this: רבי עקיבא says you say הבדלה as a fourth blessing on its own. רבי חנינא בן גמליאל says you say it in the הודאה blessing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 23. The הבדלה ruling is not really רבי אליעזר's own view, so it does not add to the list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The list only counts rulings that belong to רבי אליעזר himself. Here, רבי אליעזר was passing on a teaching from רבי חנינא בן גמליאל. The ברייתא proves that רבי חנינא בן גמליאל holds this exact view, so the ruling that follows it is really following him.

keyTerms.meaning: In the name of. Repeating someone else's teaching.
Separating שבת from the weekday. Here it means the words added in the עמידה on מוצאי שבת.
A fourth blessing on its own. A separate blessing just for הבדלה.
The thanksgiving blessing (מודים) of the עמידה.

steps.whatToRemember: The ruling about הבדלה in הודאה does not count against the list. רבי אליעזר was only repeating the view of רבי חנינא בן גמליאל.
steps.confusionAlert: The list is not changing its rule. It still counts only rulings that come from רבי אליעזר himself. This case simply turns out to be someone else's teaching.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abba said:
That one, he said it
phrases.notes: "That one" means רבי אליעזר's ruling about הבדלה from the last step.

phrases.english: in the name of Rabbi Chanina ben Gamliel,
as it is taught in a baraita:
Rabbi Akiva says:
One says it as a fourth blessing by itself;
Rabbi Chanina ben Gamliel says:
One says it in the thanksgiving blessing.
phrases.notes: This is the מודים blessing near the end of the עמידה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא: הָהוּא דְּאָמַר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 23 about הבדלה in the הודאה blessing.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attribution: the ruling is shown to belong to a different תנא, so it is not counted as following רבי אליעזר.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי אלעזר's ruling on הבדלה seemed to follow רבי אליעזר, which would be one more case on the list.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי אליעזר was repeating רבי חנינא בן גמליאל's view, so the ruling really follows רבי חנינא בן גמליאל and the list is not broken.
steps.raayaObject: That the view of saying הבדלה in הודאה belongs to רבי חנינא בן גמליאל.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא recording the dispute between רבי עקיבא and רבי חנינא בן גמליאל.
